title: Apollo 13: Explosion 200,000 Miles From Earth, and All 3 Came Home

scenes.text: An oxygen tank exploded 200,000 miles from Earth.
April 13, 1970. Heading for the Moon, Jim Lovell radioed, Houston, we've had a problem.
The crew moved into the lunar module, built to keep two men alive for 45 hours. It had to keep three alive.
Water rations dropped to a fifth, and the cabin fell to a few degrees above freezing.
Engineers built an air-filter adapter from parts already on board.
Four minutes of radio silence before reentry, then parachutes. All three came home.

description:
An oxygen tank exploded on Apollo 13 on April 13, 1970, more than 200,000 miles from Earth.
The crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat, rationed water to a fifth, and improvised an air-filter adapter before splashing down safely on April 17.
Which part of this story amazes you most? Comment below.
first_comment: The lunar module was built for two men for 45 hours and kept three alive for about four days. What would you have packed for that trip?
